title: Semi-supervised image classifiers lead to confirmation of a new lensed quasar
summary: Semi-supervised image classifiers trained on Pan-STARRS and DESI imagery surfaced five quasar-lens candidates for Keck follow-up. Spectroscopy confirmed GRALJ140833.73+042229.98 as a previously undiscovered gravitationally lensed quasar: a z=2.998 quasar lensed by a z=0.542 early-type galaxy. Three other targets were quasar-plus-star or quasar-plus-galaxy interlopers, and one remained unresolved.
ai_technology: Semi-supervised image-classifier pipeline using a convolutional autoencoder with a classifier, plus a convolutional network trained with virtual adversarial training
organization: University of Sydney; University of California, Irvine; California Institute of Technology; collaborators

evidence.tested: Semi-supervised image classifiers trained on Pan-STARRS and DESI imagery surfaced five quasar-lens candidates for Keck follow-up.
evidence.unknown: Only one of five observed candidates was confirmed; three were interlopers and one could not be resolved. The successful identification came from a previous model iteration during model development, so this is an AI-assisted discovery with limited follow-up yield, not a prospective performance demonstration.
evidence.ai_role: Image-only classifiers prioritized candidate lenses; a prior iteration of the autoencoder-classifier surfaced the object, which Keck spectroscopy subsequently confirmed. The paper notes the observed candidates were selected during model development, not from a strictly prospective frozen-model test.
